# Type exits

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

How words leave: at speed into the cut, collapsing, eroding or carried off by the camera; never a slow fade on a statement. 10 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Exit by accelerating shrink or recede

`dv-shrink-exit` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · any

A held word or text card leaves by scaling down about its centre on an ease-in (60 % of the shrink in the last 10 %), the pane easing back with it, then a hard cut (or one near-white frame); a tagline recedes and fades in 3 frames; the last word shrinks and dims like it is moving away.

- **Build:** Words exit 'launch' on scale (or a camera push-out on E.buildIn) cut on its last frame. Anatomy: Scale 1 -> 0.85-0.9 accelerating; dim 30 % on a decrescendo. Sound: A cut on the voice phrase; a boom or reverse on the decrescendo.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** 20-40 f; 14 px/f at the cut.
- **Use when:** Text cards between scenes; the last word of a section.
- **Avoid when:** Shrinking toward zero (stop at 0.85-0.9 and cut).

### Line leaves at speed into the cut

`ty-launch-exit-into-cut` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy any · any · also `dv-launch-exit`

A statement does not fade away: it accelerates out at full opacity and the film cuts on its fastest frame, carrying that speed into the next shot.

- **Build:** exit="launch" exitAt={cutFrame} exitDir="left" (or 'up') on Words or Chain: the line accelerates on E.launchIn over outDur (17 f@60 calm, 14 crisp), 1.25 em, opacity 1 to the last frame. exitAt is the last frame drawn; the next shot starts on exitAt + 1 and opens carried at 0.4-1.4 x the cut speed (lib/handoff.ts carriedCut() or carryChain()). Give `out` too to cut mid-move, before the curve ends. exitOrder 'rtl' removes the words right to left 2 f@60 apart. declares() returns the velocity seam: add it to SEAMS. Without a cut use exit="launchFade" (E.buildIn, 0.6 em, a 10 f fade in the move's last half). For a TypeLine: `exit: 'slide'` (E.buildIn, 1.5 em in 22 f, the last three words dropping off right to left 2 f apart before the cut) or `exit: 'drift'` (up and away, never faded).
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`, `fx/Words`, `fx/Chain`
- **Timing:** 8-12 f at 30 fps (17-24 f@60); 100-170 px of travel; 23-110 px/f on the last frame at 1080p; the next element visible on the first frame after the cut, or already on the line's last frame (exitOverlap 1: one frame of overlap, the seam moves with it).
- **Use when:** Every statement that hands over to a new shot; title cards before a scene change.
- **Avoid when:** A line that stays for the end lock; small UI labels (they fade in 3-6 f).

### Reading-order word exit

`ty-reading-order-exit` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy any · any

Words leave one by one in reading order, each lifting a few pixels and vanishing, until only the hero element is left on screen.

- **Build:** For each word except the hero, o_i = out + 4i and q = prog(f, o_i, o_i + 10, E.in): translateY = -depart(q) x 0.12 em, opacity = 1 - prog(f, o_i, o_i + 10, E.smooth) (never fade on E.in, which pops), blur = blurOut(q, 4). The hero word, icon or pill stays put, and the next move (zoom, match cut) starts from it within 6 f of the last word clearing. Loosen variant for a calm handoff: words drift apart vertically by sign_i x (10 + 10 x rand(i)) px with a rotation of +-2 degrees, fade toward the ground colour first (mixColor(C.ink, C.mist)) and then to 0, over 20 f on E.smooth, 6 f apart.
- **Timing:** Per word 10 f, lift 0.12 em (about 14 px), stagger 4 f (2-6), a 5-word line clears in about 26 f; loosen variant 20 f per word, 6 f apart, about 32-44 f in all.
- **Use when:** Isolating a hero word or object before a match cut or zoom; clearing a statement gently before a calmer UI moment; mirroring a word-by-word entry.
- **Avoid when:** Walkthrough captions just before a camera move: fade the whole caption at once over 26 f on E.smooth and finish 0-56 f before the move starts; exits that would hurry a payoff line.

### Words or items drop out one by one

`dv-ordered-drop-out` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · any

A line or a set leaves in a designed order: words vanish from the end one frame apart while the line accelerates; words are removed one per frame until one remains; the dim line erases word by word while the big type drifts; chips fall off while words drop right to left; words spread apart and fade from the end while the camera zooms; alternate words drop out, then the rest; list lines slide out top first; image tiles cut off one at a time.

- **Build:** Words/Chain exit with exitOrder 'rtl' (2 f apart) or 'stagger'; HardStep for one-per-frame removals. Anatomy: 1-4 f between removals; order right-to-left, alternate, top-first or noun-last; optional drift on an ease-in under it. Sound: Mouse clicks; a deep boom; clicks on the drop-outs. Materials: Two more constructions: words defocus out one at a time from the line's end (blur 0 -> 8 px with opacity 1 -> 0 over 16 f, staggered 8-12 f) while the word gaps widen 40 %; or a list turns grey, then each line is cropped away from the left by a hard edge, top lines first, so the left edge forms a staircase (24 f) as the lines fade. For a TypeLine: `exit: 'slide'` carries the right-to-left drop-out on a sideways launch.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`, `fx/Words`
- **Materials:** Two more constructions: words defocus out one at a time from the line's end (blur 0 -> 8 px with opacity 1 -> 0 over 16 f, staggered 8-12 f) while the word gaps widen 40 %; or a list turns grey, then each line is cropped away from the left by a hard edge, top lines first, so the left edge forms a staircase (24 f) as the lines fade.
- **Timing:** 14-30 f.
- **Use when:** Exits that should read as a build in reverse; leaving one word alone.
- **Avoid when:** All at once (that is a cut, not an exit).

### Short stepped or accelerating fade-out

`dv-short-fade-exit` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · any

When a fade is right, it is short and shaped: secondary labels fade out with an accelerating opacity, staggered, as the main element arrives; a phrase goes translucent on one frame and is gone on the next; text fades in five equal steps the frame before a colour beat; a caption fades as the picture fills the frame over it.

- **Build:** Words exit 'launchFade' with a short outDur, or HardStep opacity steps. Anatomy: Ease-in opacity over 4-14 f; 2-frame exit; 5 linear steps. Sound: None; the next element's sound.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** 4-30 f.
- **Use when:** Secondary text clearing the stage for the hero; text under a growing picture.
- **Avoid when:** Long linear fades of the main line.

### Tracking collapses into the cut

`ty-tracking-collapse-exit` · typography in motion · accent · energy any · any

A held line contracts toward its centre, letter spacing collapsing faster and faster with each glyph smeared toward the edge it left, and is cut while it moves.

- **Build:** From `out`: p = E.buildIn((f - out) / 10); each glyph moves -12 % of its distance from the line's centre x p; a trail of that frame's travel toward the edge. Cut on frame 10 (about 9 % narrower on the last frame shown). For a TypeLine: `exit: 'collapse'`.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`
- **Timing:** 10 f (4-5 f at 30 fps); 9-12 % narrower at the cut.
- **Use when:** A caption that should leave without a direction, sucked into the next shot (a search field, a chip, a mark at the centre).
- **Avoid when:** Long lines (the outer glyphs travel too far); a line that should be read again.

### Words blur out and vanish

`dv-blur-fade-exit` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · any

Text softens and fades together (blur to about 40 px with opacity on one clock), often followed by exactly one empty frame; or the previous words turn grey and blurred and stay behind the new ones as a ghost.

- **Build:** <DefocusCut out empty={1}>; the ghost as a RackFocus level kept behind the new line. Anatomy: Blur 8-40 px and opacity together, most of the blur late; one empty frame; ghost variant: grey, blurred, held behind. Sound: A level swell before the cut; a quiet breath.
- **Primitive:** `fx/CutFx.DefocusCut`
- **Timing:** 8-18 f; empty 1 f.
- **Use when:** Calm statements leaving; a line that should feel spoken into silence.
- **Avoid when:** Blur on small UI type; a hero line or a statement (they leave at speed: slide, drift, spread, collapse).

### Words float away; the hub stays

`dv-hub-stays` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

All the words drift up on an ease-in and disappear, while an icon stays exactly in place and gains a rounded container: it becomes the hub of the next scene.

- **Build:** Words exit 'launch' upward; Morph box around the icon. Anatomy: Words up 1 -> 12 px/f; the icon fixed; the container grows around it. Sound: An onset as the container appears.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** 16-22 f.
- **Use when:** Turning a statement into the product's centre.
- **Avoid when:** Moving the hub.

### Words track apart into a zoom

`ty-tracking-spread-exit` · typography in motion · accent · energy high · any

The line leaves by its words tracking apart faster and faster while the camera zooms toward the first word; the words go from the end, right to left, and the cut lands on the peak.

- **Build:** From `out`: q = (f - out) / 26; word w moves +0.5 em x w x E.launchIn(q); the line scales x1.6^E.launchIn(q) about the first word's centre; word w (rank r from the last) fades over 8 f from 26 x (0.4 + 0.45 r / (n - 1)) f. Cut on frame 26 (the first words still show). For a TypeLine: `exit: 'spread'`.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`
- **Timing:** 26 f; word drift 0.5 em per word index; zoom x1.6 (x2.3 when the camera carries on into the next shot); fades 8 f, right to left.
- **Use when:** A line that hands over to a bigger moment (a drop, a product reveal) through a zoom; typed lines that should leave as typing became motion.
- **Avoid when:** A quiet line before a hold; two tracking exits in one film.

### An object sweeps through and eats the text

`dv-object-eats-text` · typography in motion · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

Something solid erases the words as it passes: a bar of the word's height sweeps across the keyword; a rule grows from the caret and the letters turn the accent and vanish one by one; a button slides over the line and the word disappears from its leading edge; an app icon slides to centre and the text left of it is clipped into its edge.

- **Build:** Build: <Knockout at from to text x y font mode="clip"|"letters"|"reveal" object="bar"|"rule"|(edgeX) => node accent> (fx/Knockout): one closed-form edge (24 f on E.softIn) clips the text at the object's leading edge; letters removes whole letters as the edge passes their centres (about 3 f apart), each lit in the accent just before it goes; reveal writes the line on behind the object. Anatomy: Clip edge = the object's leading edge; letters 3 f apart; partial letters visible at the edge. Sound: A whoosh tail.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Knockout`
- **Timing:** 8-58 f.
- **Use when:** Replacing a word with a product action; deleting the old way.
- **Avoid when:** Objects that do not belong to the product.
